analysis:
The only change in StandaloneServer+NativeMiMo.swift is in buildNativeMiMoCandidate (head lines 372-376). EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants now receives an extra argument, minimumGrantBytes: Self.minimumGrantBytes(existing). This is a KV-grant sizing/availability parameter for the native MiMo load. The surrounding Standalone native-owner lifecycle is unchanged: checkNativeMiMoSetupOwner checks, the resliceKeepsSlotsServiceable guard at head line 377, previousGrants restore, retirement/fence logic and the shrink-then-grow ordering of grants at head lines 383-388 and 435-440.

I saw no change to the data flows that matter for the threat model: the E2E encryption path (A-001, TB-002), the attestation and App Attest authorization paths (TB-009, TB-011), the SSD prefix cache (T-041), and the cache-hash gating at head lines 319-354. That gating still uses the cryptographic weight-hash bracket and still disables reusable SSD cache when the hash is unavailable or changed. The new parameter does not touch cache scope, salt, TTL or key derivation, and it adds no new attack surface or trust-boundary crossing.

Open questions for integration, which I could not verify from the supplied evidence: the definition of Self.minimumGrantBytes(existing) and the new minimumGrantBytes behavior in EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants were not provided. If the minimum is computed incorrectly, it could affect the serviceability floor and availability, but resliceKeepsSlotsServiceable is still checked afterwards and would refuse the load. That is a correctness/availability matter at most, not a demonstrated security regression. A reviewer of those unseen files should confirm that the minimum is bounded and cannot cause the grants to exceed the fleet KV budget (memory exhaustion, T-029-style).

No findings.
